figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1.   Phylogenic analysis of genes in the IC-­based pathway across plant species. (A) Phylogenetic tree of the plant species analyzed in this study. The proposed times 
for At-­α and At-­β WGD events are shown. (B–D) Phylogenic trees of ICS (B), EDS5 (C), and PBS3 (D) homologs from various plant species. Mya, million years ago. Trees 
were generated based on full-­length amino acid sequences using the maximum likelihood method. Triangles represent collapsed branches. The scale bar denotes a 
phylogenetic distance of amino acid substitutions per site. Bootstrap values, derived from 1,000 replications, are indicated at branch nodes. Red-­colored genes indicate 
genes that were experimentally tested in this study. Genes with filled circles were highly functional for SA biosynthesis in this study. (D) Clade A contains Subclade A1 
and A2. Subclade A1 is divided into Subclade A1a (AtPBS3 clade) and A1b. Some illustrations were created using BioRender. (For more detailed phylogenetic trees, 
see Datasets S1–S3.)

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.   Characterization of A. thaliana ICS1 mutants. (A and B) Agrobacterium strains carrying A. thaliana ICS-­Myc (or mutated ICS-­Myc), EDS5-­YFP, and PBS3-­YFP 
were coinfiltrated into leaves of 4 to 6-­wk-­old N. benthamiana plants. SA and SAG levels in leaf extracts were quantified at 5 dpi. Data represent means ± SEM 
from 4 biological replicates. Asterisks indicate significant differences compared to EV (*P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, and ***P < 0.001, two-­tailed Student’s t test). (C) 
Agrobacterium strains carrying ICS1-­YFP were infiltrated into N. benthamiana leaves. ICS1 subcellular localization in epidermal cells was analyzed by confocal 
microscopy at 2 dpi. (Scale bar, 20 µm.) (D) Structural model of A. thaliana ICS1 and C. papaya ICS1 predicted by AlphaFold2. The overall structure of AtICS1 and 
close-­up views of the salt bridge network (AtICS1 and CpICS) are shown. Putative hydrogen bonds are represented by dotted lines. IC from the EntC structure 
(PDB ID: 3HWO) was superimposed onto the predicted AtICS1 and CpICS structures. (E) Agrobacterium strains carrying ICS-­YFP were infiltrated into N. benthamiana 
leaves. Total protein was extracted from the infiltrated leaves at 2 dpi, and ICS protein expression was assessed by immunoblotting using an anti-­Myc antibody.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4.   Brassicales PBS3 homologs, except for that from C. papaya, are functional for SA biosynthesis. Agrobacterium strains carrying PBS3-­YFP from various 
species were coinfiltrated with Agrobacterium strains carrying A. thaliana ICS-­Myc and EDS5-­YFP into leaves of 4 to 6-­wk-­old N. benthamiana plants. (A–D) SA and 
SAG levels in leaf extracts were quantified at 5 dpi. “−” represents the empty vector control. Data represent means ± SEM from 4 biological replicates. Asterisks 
indicate significant differences compared to EV (*P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, and ***P < 0.001, two-­tailed Student’s t test). (E) Agrobacterium strains carrying PBS3-­YFP 
were infiltrated into N. benthamiana leaves. PBS3 subcellular localization in epidermal cells expressing PBS3-­YFP was analyzed by confocal microscopy at 2 dpi. 
(Scale bar, 20 µm.) (F) Agrobacterium strains carrying PBS3-­YFP were infiltrated into N. benthamiana leaves. EV represents the empty vector control. Total protein 
was extracted from the infiltrated leaves at 2 dpi, and PBS3 protein expression was assessed by immunoblotting using an anti-­GFP antibody.
